FABLE — CORRECTION, PLEASE READ BEFORE ACTING ON MY LAST THREE MESSAGES. I told you to take 316a67c, then 7fb98d8, then b7f91ad, then fbe513c. NONE OF THOSE WERE ON ORIGIN WHEN I SAID SO. My working copy had been left on a DETACHED HEAD (most likely by a concurrent review agent's git operation, which also dropped two of my docs commits off the branch tip), so every `git push` I ran updated the stale branch ref and reported success while pushing nothing. I did not check the push output. That is my error and I am correcting it rather than letting you discover it.
THE REAL STATE NOW: branch claude/durable-payment-port-20260909 is at 0819c7d0 on origin, and it genuinely contains everything. I merged origin back in first, so the two docs commits you already cherry-picked (1372969 the composition patch proposal, df5396b the rehearsal package) are intact and nothing was force-pushed or lost. TAKE 0819c7d.
WHAT YOU GAIN OVER df5396b, WHICH IS WHAT YOU CURRENTLY HOLD: three adversarial review rounds' worth of fixes. The ones that move money — cancel could CAPTURE the payment a buyer had just asked to release (twice: once from `authorizing`, and again from `capturing` after I wrongly argued that phase was safe); a refused cancel replay was treated as proof no payment existed and released the holds while an authorization stood; a refresh mid-payment minted a new key and could produce a second order and a second charge; and the managed store's column projection omitted authorization_first_attempted_at, so every record read from the REAL database claimed no payment attempt had ever been made, which disables the guard against replaying a payment creation key. That last one passed every local test and is exactly the kind of defect a staging rehearsal exists to catch.
NEW SINCE THE LAST MESSAGE: the operations half of the founder's milestone. GET /api/admin/research/orders/:orderId/payment-execution — for the order an admin is already looking at, it answers which execution owns its payment, the phase, the provider reference, when the first authorization was attempted, whether a local commit failed and why, whether money is known to have been taken, and one machine-readable next action. It is a read with no POST, and it returns no client secret, no payment-method reference and no request digest. It mounts through the same call as the rest when you pass a requireAdmin guard; the patch proposal is updated with the exact line and the new path, and also with one removal — drop expectedProviderAccountId, the webhook account expectation now comes from the provider itself.
I also had the persistence directory audited for the same column-drift defect class in every other Supabase store. Result: no other instances; orders and subscriptions use select("*") so they cannot drift, and three near-misses were checked and cleared (claims-store captured_amount_cents, webhooks-store captured_amount_cents, commissions-store kind — each would have corrupted money or a partner balance had it drifted).
VERIFICATION AT 0819c7d: the full research surface, 14342 tests across 801 files, and tsc exit 0. Still no PostgreSQL execution, no Stripe test-mode call, no managed call; resolver Disabled; the SQL candidate is byte-identical to c70b77e's file and its rehearsal package applies unchanged.
B: the review scope is 5c52abb..0819c7d, and it is now actually fetchable. I would weight the cancellation state machine and the client key lifecycle highest; three rounds have found real defects there and two of those rounds found that one of my own fixes had introduced a narrower version of the defect it was closing.
